fine_trace.code: rc = match(start_match, mb->start_code, match_data->ovector, match_data->oveccount, re->top_bracket, frame_size, mb);
fine_trace.note: The external match_data ovector (32 pairs, created by the caller) and its pair count oveccount are passed into the interpreter; oveccount is the 'available space in the external ovector'.

Each backtracking frame embeds an ovector whose capacity is derived only from re->top_bracket (number of capturing parentheses in the pattern), so the internal frame ovector has only top_bracket*2 entries.

Root cause: the copy length is computed from the external oveccount instead of the internal frame ovector capacity. When the pattern has fewer capturing parentheses than oveccount-1 (top_bracket < oveccount-1), the memcpy reads (oveccount-1)*2 entries from Fovector, which only has top_bracket*2 entries.

Sink: the memcpy reads from F->ovector (the current frame's ovector) beyond the end of the frame vector allocation when the current frame is the last one and oveccount > top_bracket+1, i.e. reading from invalid memory.

vuln_logic.issue_alignment: Reading from invalid memory occurs when the pattern has fewer capturing parentheses (top_bracket) than the available space in the external ovector (oveccount): the result-copy memcpy at the successful-match exit is sized by (oveccount-1)*2 entries and reads past the frame-embedded ovector (top_bracket*2 entries). The fix bounds the copy to 2*min(top_bracket+1, oveccount) entries.
